intent: Every engine drives a browser through one interface that tells the truth about what was applied.
change: BrowserProvider interface with SessionMeta echo contract, withBrowser() release guarantee, LocalProvider on plain Playwright chromium, the provider contract test suite, and CI wiring (chromium install) so the suite runs on every push.
done_when: Contract suite green on LocalProvider in pnpm check locally and in CI; withBrowser proven to release on success, on thrown error, and idempotently on double release; SessionMeta echoes not-applied options honestly.

proofs.claim: Before withBrowser exists the release-guarantee tests still execute, reach the seam, and fail there instead of reporting a released session.
Before LocalProvider exists the provider contract suite still executes against a real browser seam and fails at the factory instead of passing vacuously.

withBrowser releases on success, releases and re-throws the body error on failure, releases exactly once when the body released already, surfaces a release failure the body did not mask, reports one it did, and runs no body and tracks no session when acquire fails. LocalProvider turns a missing browser into a typed error naming the install command and leaves nothing tracked behind it.

The provider contract suite passes against LocalProvider on a real headless Chromium: acquire drives a page on local static content, the echo reports stealth, proxy, captcha and recording as not applied and an unattached profile as an absent storage state, withBrowser releases on success and on a thrown body, a second release is a no-op, and dispose leaves an empty ledger and refuses further acquires.
The whole repository gate stays green with the seam and its browser-driving integration suite inside it, and the documented setup names the browser-install step CI runs before the gate.

intent: Encode every Solari sharp edge once, behind the seam, so no engine is ever written against wrong vendor assumptions.
change: SolariProvider on @solarisdk/browser launch() with maxAttempts:1 and provider-owned retry, self-tracked session ledger with failed-release retention, option mapping with cross-field preflight, degradation echoes (proxy presence/tier, timezoneId, storageState tri-state), typed error taxonomy (429 non-retryable, 5xx retryable, 402/428 config), and dispose() ordering solari.close after releases.
done_when: Mocked-transport unit tests prove single-create-on-timeout, create/release/dispose ordering, ledger add/remove/retention, unproxied echo when the response omits proxy, 429 mapped non-retryable, and proxy-without-stealth preflight rejection; contract suite compiles against SolariProvider.

proofs.claim: Before SolariProvider exists the lifecycle, ledger and error-taxonomy tests still execute against the seam and fail at the factory instead of passing vacuously.

The vendor SDK's unconditional isRetryableError really does re-send POST /sessions after a client-side timeout: with SDK defaults the exactly-one-create test observes two creates, which is the duplicate billable session the provider must close.

SolariProvider maps options with cross-field preflight, echoes applied capabilities including proxy degradation, keeps a self-tracked ledger that retains failed releases, orders dispose as release-then-solari.close, and maps the documented status codes to the seam's error kinds.
The whole gate stays green with the vendor SDK added: the contract suite compiles against SolariProvider, no module outside solari.ts imports @solarisdk/browser, and coverage holds.

intent: A real vendor round-trip proves the adapter works and becomes the standing early-warning line for vendor drift.
change: @live-tagged vitest suite plus a GitHub Actions workflow (nightly schedule + manual dispatch, secrets-gated): recorded fast-pool session, stable public page assertion, rrweb flush pause, release, replay-URL poll through 404s (~30s), replay decompression finding recorded in code, empty-ledger assert, dispose; missing SOLARI_API_KEY yields an explicit skipped status.
done_when: One workflow run with the secret is green end-to-end including replay retrieval and the empty-ledger assert; one run without the secret reports skipped, not green; both runs linked from the sprint PR.

external_gate.summary: SOLARI_API_KEY must exist as a GitHub Actions secret before the nightly live smoke can run in CI. The key exists locally in .env, so the composed vendor path is proven here; only the workflow-run half of done_when waits on the secret and a push.

proofs.claim: Before the skip guard exists the missing-secret tests still execute and fail at the guard, rather than a suite that silently passes because it never ran anything.
A missing SOLARI_API_KEY yields an explicit skip reason rather than a pass, and the workflow fires only on a schedule or a manual dispatch - never on an ordinary push.

The live run found the adapter aborting every real acquire: the vendor documents a default context at contexts()[0], and a freshly launched session actually has none. A fake that hands back a context encodes the documentation, so this pins the observed shape instead - an empty contexts() must still yield a usable session.

expected.failure_signature: solari session arrived without its default context

proofs.claim: acquire() creates the context itself when the session ships without one, and still reuses the default context when the vendor does provide it.

The composed real-vendor path runs end to end against Solari through a runner that refuses to pass without a real run: a recorded fast-pool session loads a stable public page, the title asserts, release tears the session down, the replay URL arrives through its 404 window, and the provider ledger is empty afterwards.
The whole gate stays green with the live suite and its workflow added, and the live suite is excluded from the ordinary run rather than failing it.

intent: The nightly live smoke must fail as a failure rather than as a twenty-minute hang, and must hold the poll window it claims.
change: Three defects on the live-smoke surface, all inside the accepted outcome. (1) runLiveSmoke teardown awaits provider.dispose() then replayClient.close() sequentially, so a throwing dispose skips close(), leaves the SDK local proxy thread alive, and hangs the Node process instead of failing it; the same throw also replaces the body error. Settle both teardowns and re-propagate the body error, applying the discipline withBrowser already documents in packages/solari/src/provider.ts. (2) The replay client is built with no timeoutMs, so the SDK 90s default lets one hung getReplayUrl overshoot the 30s poll budget threefold; bound each attempt to the remaining window so the poll cannot outlive its own deadline. (3) The suite name carries no @live tag, though live-smoke-path.md asks for an @live-tagged suite, TEST-MATRIX.md declares the @live tier for this sprint, and packages/agent/src/live-llm.integration.test.ts already tags its suite name @live-llm.
done_when: A unit test proves a throwing dispose still closes the replay client and still propagates the body error rather than the teardown error. A unit test drives pollReplayUrl with an attempt that never settles and asserts it rejects near its timeoutMs instead of hanging. The live suite reports under a name carrying the @live tag with and without a skip reason, matching the tier the spec and TEST-MATRIX declare and the convention packages/agent already uses. (Sharpened during hardening: the original wording claimed vitest -t @live would select the suite, which is not observable while describe.skipIf skips it - the skip dominates the name filter. The tag being present is the part this task controls and the part the spec asks for.) Whole gate green.

proofs.claim: Before the teardown discipline exists the tests reach for it and fail there: runTeardowns is absent, and pollReplayUrl hangs past its own 200ms deadline instead of giving up near it.

Every teardown runs even when an earlier one throws, each failure is reported with the label of what failed, pollReplayUrl gives up near its own deadline when a single attempt never settles, and the live suite name carries the @live tag with and without a skip reason.
The live suite still loads, still reports skipped rather than green without an opt-in, and now carries the @live tag in the name it reports under.

intent: The vendor import boundary that solari-session-hygiene names as part of its claim is proven rather than trusted.
change: solari-session-hygiene.md states that SolariProvider is the only code in the system that imports @solarisdk/browser and that the import boundary is part of this spec claim. Nothing enforces it: eslint.config.js restricts only the db/drizzle/pg group for the dashboard, and no test covers the vendor SDK. Add a boundary test mirroring tests/telegram-boundary.test.ts, which already proves the one-module invariant for grammY, so the second module to reach for the vendor SDK fails the gate rather than passing quietly.
done_when: A test walks the workspace source roots and asserts packages/solari/src/solari.ts is the only module importing @solarisdk/browser. Adding that import to any other workspace file fails the test. Whole gate green.
